headlines.title: Cal Fire stops forward progress of Napa County Steele Fire
headlines.description: A brush fire burned at least 45 acres and triggered an evacuation warning Wednesday in Napa County, Cal Fire said. The so-called Steele Fire burned in a steep terrain near the 9400 block of Steele Canyon Road. An evacuation warning was issued for the areas east of Steele Canyon Road, west of Wragg Canyon Road and north of Highway 128. The evacuation warning was lifted at around 1 p.m. At 1:25 p.m., Cal Fire reported stopping forward progress of the blaze. No other information was immediately available. headlines.title: Multiple juveniles injured in alleged stabbing near San Jose Light Rail Station
headlines.description: San Jose Police officers responded to a reported stabbing involving two groups of juveniles near the Fruitdale Light Rail Station on Tuesday evening, authorities said. Officers were called to the area at approximately 6:36 p.m., according to the San Jose Police Department. Preliminary information indicates the incident occurred near the light rail station platform. Multiple victims sustained injuries, and at least one victim was taken to a hospital for treatment. The Santa Clara County Sheriff’s Office was also notified. Police said the incident remains an active and ongoing investigation and that additional information will be released as it becomes available.

headlines.title: Heat advisory in effect across Bay Area
headlines.description: The National Weather Service forecast for the greater San Francisco Bay Area for Wednesday calls for hot conditions, especially inland, with mostly sunny skies during the day and a lot of cloud cover at night. Daytime highs will be mostly in the high 70s to mid 90s on the coast, in the high 80s to mid 90s around the bay, and in the high 90s to mid 100s inland. Overnight lows will be mostly in the mid to high 60s with some interior areas reaching the low 70s. Forecasters say the Bay Area will remain hot Wednesday as moisture from the remnants of Marie moves north over the region, bringing more high and middle clouds. A Heat Advisory remains in effect across the region through 10 p.m. Thursday. Strong high pressure is expected to push morning lows higher and bring daytime temps into the 90s to lower 100s across much of the area. High to middle clouds are expected to spread on Wednesday. The NWS says radar detected light, high-based showers, with isolated lightning observed southwest of Bay Area. Forecasters say that along the immediate coast, the afternoon sea breeze could lower temps somewhat. With heat continuing, the weather service recommends limiting unnecessary outdoor activity, taking breaks in the shade, using air conditioning, and drinking cool water. Never leave children or pets in parked cars, or leave pets or livestock without shade and water.

headlines.title: San Jose leaders to give recommendations to rename former Plaza de Cesar Chavez
headlines.description: Parks and Recreation leaders in San Jose are scheduled to give their recommendation to rename the city’s most popular plaza. The city removed the Plaza de Cesar Chavez name shortly after the allegations of sexual abuse emerged in March about the late labor leader. The new options are down to two: Plaza de San Jose or Farmworkers Plaza. The commission originally planned to recommend a new name on Sept. 2 but then canceled that meeting and rescheduled it for Wednesday night. Council members will make the final decision likely next month.

headlines.title: BART reports systemwide delay due to equipment problems
headlines.description: BART is reporting a major systemwide delay Wednesday due to equipment problems. The delay was first reported on the San Francisco Line in the East Bay, SFO Airport, Millbrae and Daly City directions. The delay is caused by equipment problems on the track near the Daly City and West Oakland stations. BART officials didn’t describe the equipment problems or provide an estimated time for when the delay will be resolved. Other unrelated incidents also caused delays Wednesday morning, according to transit officials. At 8:15 a.m., a fire near West Oakland caused delays, while a medical emergency aboard an SFO-bound train during the 9 a.m. hour also impacted service. BART officials also reported limited Green line service between Berryessa and MacArthur station. Passengers traveling from the San Francisco line can board a Blue Line train and transfer at Bayfair for serive to Berryessa. People traveling from the Berryessa line can board a Green or Orange Line train and transfer at Bayfair station to a Blue line Daly City train. BART also reported limited Blue line service between Dublin/Pleasanton and 24th/Mission stations. Passengers traveling from the San Francisco line can board an Antioch or Richmond train and transfer at 24th St Mission to the Blue line train.

headlines.title: New development at SF's former Candlestick Park site to bring new homes
headlines.description: A major groundbreaking was held in San Francisco Wednesday for the new waterfront community development around the former Candlestick Park Stadium site. Candlestick Park was demolished in 2015, but there has been a series of hurdles to development over the years. Mayor Daniel Lurie was at the groundbreaking, along with Congresswoman Nancy Pelosi, and other prominent local leaders. The plan now is to create more than 7,000 new homes in the Bayview District, including affordable units. The developer calls it an innovation district, shops, restaurants and parks and public access to more than two miles of waterfront space. “For years, San Franciscans heard about what would someday rise at Candlestick. They heard about new homes and parks and shops jobs, but year after year it remained empty. Today, I am proud that we are breaking ground at Candlestick and taking the first step toward 7,200 new homes in San Francisco,” Lurie said. The plan also calls for several public spaces and streets to be named after key figures with San Francisco Giants and 49ers including Willie Mays and Joe Montana

headlines.title: ‘Never forget,' 25 years later: Betty Ong, the flight attendant who made the first 9/11 call
headlines.description: On the morning of Sept. 11, 2001, American Airlines flight attendant Betty Ann Ong was the first person to sound the alarm about the tragedy that was about to unfold. The San Francisco native was based at Logan International Airport in Massachusetts and was aboard Flight 11 bound for Los Angeles with 92 people on board when hijackers took over the plane. “My name is Betty Ong, I’m number three on Flight 11,” Ong said in a call to the American Airlines reservation center in Raleigh, North Carolina. “The cockpit’s not answering. Somebody’s stabbed in business class and — I think there’s mace — we can’t breathe. I don’t know, I think we’re getting hijacked.” Ong remained on the phone for 23 minutes, relaying information about what was unfolding onboard until the plane she was on careened into the World Trade Center’s North Tower at 8:46 a.m. That call led air traffic controllers to land every plane flying over the U.S. Her bravery on that day made her a national hero. Twenty-five years later, Ong’s name and legacy lives on in San Francisco’s Chinatown where she grew up, and in the heart of her older brother, Harry Ong, who grieves for the litte sister he called “Bee.” “It still hurts. You almost die 25 times,” Harry Ong said. “Every year you hope that America and the world won’t forget 9/11, yet you yourself want to forget 9/11.” Harry said his wife woke him up that morning and they watched the news unfold on TV, but didn’t know Betty was on that plane. “I didn’t know until about 7 o’clock our time. And I just called American Airlines, kept calling them for about five, six times. And finally, they acknowledged that Betty may have been on that flight,” Harry said. Betty wasn’t supposed to be on that flight. She picked up an extra shift to earn money for an upcoming trip with her sisters, Cathie and Gloria. “When she didn’t call back, after we’ve left messages on her cell phone to please call and contact us, and she never returned a call, our hearts were sinking fast,” Harry recalled. Harry then had call his parents to tell deliver the heartbreaking news. Twenty-five years later, Harry says he’s still not at peace with her passing. “My feeling as her elder brother and the only brother in our culture was to protect her, and I had somehow had this feeling of just failing her,” he said. Harry said the family is still proud of what she did that day, adding “she did her duty and her professionalism showed.” Betty Ann Ong grew up in Chinatown. She worked in her parents market on Jackson Street. And, when they decided to retire in 1987, she set out to travel and see the world, and became a flight attendant. Today, Betty’s memory is carried on through the Betty Ann Ong Foundation and at the Betty Ann Ong Chinese Recreation Center in the neighborhood her family called home and where she once played. “This was really her playground. And she would come up here whenever she didn’t have any homework or school,” Harry said. The center was rebuilt and renamed, and now holds year-round programs for seniors and children in the community. It also hosts three big holiday parties every year in honor of Betty. Her name is everywhere at the center, on the walls and on posters, and on a bronze plaque hanging in the entrance for all to see as they walk in. “Just never forget, never forget Betty. Never forget all those who are lost,” Harry said. “I always remember and pray for flight attendants wherever they are, wherever they may be, and I just hope that people will never forget 9/11.”
headlines.source: Jessica Aguirre, Christine Ni and Jeremy Carroll

headlines.title: Pittsburg police station shooting suspect appears in court
headlines.description: A man accused of shooting a Pittsburg police officer inside police headquarters last week made his first court appearance Wednesday to face four felony counts, including attempted murder. Police Chief Phil Galer said the suspect, identified as 31-year-old Michael Sanchez Gardner Martin, concealed a gun in his clothing after an arresting officer failed to find it during two searches. Martin was charged Martin was arrested Thursday afternoon on suspicion of driving a stolen vehicle and other outstanding felony warrants, according to police. He was taken to police headquarters and placed in a holding cell. Police said Martin told Officer Jimmy Sanchez, who was not involved in the arrest or searches, that he was not feeling well and needed water. Pittsburg Sep 8 Pittsburg Sep 4 Pittsburg Sep 3 Martin allegedly had the gun concealed beneath a blanket draped over his shoulders when Sanchez brought him water, according to police. Police said Martin punched Sanchez, threw the blanket over the officer’s head and struck him in the head with the gun before firing one shot. The bullet went through Martin’s thigh and struck Sanchez in the stomach below his body armor, according to police. The wounded officer and others then managed to disarm Martin. In a show of support, about two dozen Pittsburg police officers appeared in Wednesday’s arraignment. “It’s rare that shots are fired on a police officer in this county, but it does happen and it’s horrible so that’s why we see so many officers out here in support of the injured officer,” Contra Costa County Deputy District Attorney Kevin Bell said. Martin is an alleged gang member who previously served an eight-year prison sentence for manslaughter. He is scheduled to enter a plea on September 23. If convicted of all four felony counts, Martin could face 60 years to life in prison. The officer who was shot underwent surgery and is now said to be recovering with his family.

headlines.title: 20-year-old arrested after father fatally stabbed in Castro Valley
headlines.description: An Alameda County man died over the weekend after allegedly being stabbed by his adult son who was trying to protect his mother during “a family disturbance,” according to law enforcement officials. At about 1:30 p.m., sheriff’s deputies were sent to a home in the 1800 block of Parsons Avenue in the unincorporated community of Castro Valley. When they got to the scene, they found a 51-year-old man who had been stabbed. He was taken to the hospital, where he later died. His name was not immediately released. Deputies arrested his 20-year-old son on suspicion of murder after he allegedly intervened “in a physical altercation” between his parents and stabbed his father, according to sheriff’s officials.

headlines.title: Antioch schools face fire watch after custodian warns of malfunctioning alarms
headlines.description: A custodian in the Antioch Unified School District is raising alarms over what he calls an immediate safety crisis, warning that a majority of local schools lack properly functioning fire alarm systems. Jacob Ferguson, a school custodian, said he grew concerned after the school district recently eliminated the electronics technician position responsible for maintaining the fire alarm systems across its campuses. System panels at several locations were seen beeping and flashing warning lights indicating malfunctions. “It’s either shut off or blinking red an alarm in trouble,” Ferguson said. “As of today, I would say a good 80% of all of our sites do not have functioning fire alarm systems.” Ferguson warned that the lack of working alarms puts students at direct risk. “By not having the systems working, we’re basically allowing our children to ride in our car without seatbelts, which is disgusting to me,” Ferguson said. Following inquiries, the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District sent an inspector to Black Diamond Middle School and two other campuses. Fire officials noted they were aware of some pre-existing issues but not the full scope, prompting them to escalate their response and formally place two schools, including Black Diamond Middle School, on official fire watch status due to major system issues. “The functioning that would alert people on site of a problem is fully functional,” said Capt. George Laing of the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District. “The part that’s not functional is communication to the fire department.” Under a formal fire watch, a dedicated person must continuously patrol the campus until the communications system is repaired. In a statement addressing the concerns, the Antioch Unified School District said: “We are actively working to resolve the situation and have contracted a fire watch service to cover the affected sites until the issue is resolved.” Laing emphasized the department’s priority regarding campus safety. “We share the community’s concern and we prioritize the safety of children above most others,” Laing said. Fire officials confirmed that the school district will have the fire alarm systems across all 20-plus of its sites inspected by an outside contractor.

headlines.title: Bay Area students testing driverless race cars
headlines.description: Imagine riding in a Waymo, but at 150 mph. That’s what some Bay Area students are working toward on some of America’s best-known racetracks. The cars with no drivers are racing at speeds up to 155 mph, with some being tested at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca in Salinas. Some of the students testing the cars are from the University of California, Berkeley. NBC Bay Area business and tech reporter Scott Budman has more in the video above. headlines.title: Woman held on $500K bail in Richmond standoff that left officer wounded
headlines.description: A 39-year-old woman is being held on $500,000 bail after allegedly firing more than 30 rounds from a rifle during a standoff last week, wounding a responding police officer and striking a patrol vehicle and nearby homes, police said Tuesday. Jasmine Robinson of Richmond faces suspicion of attempted murder, assault with an assault weapon and kidnapping, according to the Richmond Police Department. The shooting occurred around 6:41 p.m. on Sept. 3 when officers accompanied Contra Costa County’s Behavioral Health Crisis Response Team, known as A3, on a mental health check in the 2200 block of Key Boulevard in Richmond. Officer Church, a 25-year department veteran, was struck by gunfire shortly after arriving at the scene. He was treated at a local trauma center and released Sept. 4 to recover at home. A second officer inside a struck patrol car, A3 personnel and neighboring residents escaped injury, police reported. “We are thankful that despite the extraordinary level of gunfire and danger presented during this incident, our officer survived, our A3 partners were unharmed, and no members of our community were injured,” the department said in a statement. Authorities said Robinson barricaded herself inside the home, indiscriminately firing a Romarm/Cugir Draco-C rifle. “The significant threat posed by the suspect required a large-scale tactical response, including armored rescue vehicles and specialized resources from allied law enforcement agencies,” the department said. “These resources were critical in allowing personnel to safely respond to an exceptionally dangerous and unpredictable situation and ultimately take the suspect into custody.” SWAT officers, crisis negotiators, chemical agents and armored rescue vehicles from multiple allied agencies safely evacuated neighbors and forced Robinson’s surrender. “Their professionalism, teamwork, and willingness to place themselves in harm’s way were instrumental in bringing this incident to a safe conclusion,” the department added. Additional charges against Robinson are anticipated as the investigation continues.
